quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while riding?

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: What fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding?

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A change in handling may mean a tire has failed. If your motorcycle does not handle normally, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should motorcycle riders watch for?

options.text: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked vehicles. Watch for cars pulling away from the curb or leaving parking spaces.

questions.question: What should you do if a driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to let them share it.

questions.explanation: The safest way to handle tailgating is to let the other vehicle pass you. If you can do so safely, change lanes and let them go ahead. Speeding up may make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider improve visibility?
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials. Also use your headlight at all times and use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: When you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: You don't need to check tire pressure.
Expect it to handle like your own bike.
The owner will check the brakes for you.
Leave extra space between you and other vehicles to give yourself more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space between you and other vehicles to give yourself more time to react.
questions.explanation: When borrowing a motorcycle, do all the same safety checks you would on your own bike. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar motorcycle and keep extra distance when stopping.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols are warning signs. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles do?

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Keeps you in one spot in the lane and limits your movement.
Lets you rely on others to spot hazards.
Requires you to drive faster to stay with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Leaving space around your motorcycle helps you have enough time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of having an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend in with traffic so other drivers do not notice you.
Not use turn signals unless you are riding at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Follow closely behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Tell them what you plan to do by using your turn signals and brake lights. Keep enough distance between you and other vehicles. Look ahead 12 seconds down the road. Be ready to react if danger appears.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Use proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle can still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle can pass if the pass is completed before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle can pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Do not pass in no passing zones. Also, do not pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ride faster to get away from them.
Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Riding faster may make them follow you at a higher speed, which creates more danger.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.explanation: To estimate remaining alcohol, subtract the hours since drinking from the total drinks consumed. In this case, four drinks would remain in the system.

questions.question: Which of the following colors is best for being seen while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible while riding. Wear bright clothing no matter what time of day you ride.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. The brakes work best when used together.

questions.question: ____ is the only way to remove alcohol and its effects from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time and not drinking alcohol will lower your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot reduce your blood alcohol level or make you sober. They may help keep you awake, but they do not change your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If possible, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to continue tailgating at a higher speed, creating more danger.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, their effects:

options.text: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
Are less dangerous than when either is used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can see other vehicle lights better.
Harder than riding during the day because you cannot see as well.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than riding during the day because you cannot see as well.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because you cannot see and be seen as well as during the day. Without natural light and shadows, it is difficult to judge distances.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Proper protection includes a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not provide this protection.

questions.question: You have had alcohol to drink. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still be present in your body.
You will be safe as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present in your body.
questions.explanation: The body removes about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can still build up in your body even if you drink one drink per hour. Your abilities and judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only during the day.
Be worn both day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn both day and night.
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps you be seen at any time. Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, so wearing bright clothing during the day is also important.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of having an accident, you should:

options.text: Ride within one foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Signal only when you want to.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Signal your turns and lane changes. Use your brake light. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside your motorcycle.
